request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: Unknown

Age: 75 years

Date of Admission: Unknown

Date of Discharge: Unknown
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]Principal Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Clinical Presentation:

The patient, who had a medical history of hypertension, was admitted to the hospital with a complaint of fecal occult blood. A colonoscopy revealed a type II tumor in the sigmoid colon, which was located 23 cm from the anal verge. Histopathology of a biopsy specimen revealed moderately differentiated tubular adenocarcinoma. CT imaging showed sigmoid colon wall thickening, and regional lymph node metastasis was suspected. Blood examination showed an elevated carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) concentration (32.7 ng/ml).

Hospital Course:

The patient underwent a laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy, which was performed without complications. Postoperative histopathological examination revealed moderately differentiated to mucinous adenocarcinoma, and three of the 16 retrieved lymph nodes contained malignant cells. The cancer was classified as stage IIIb [pT4a, pN1b, M0]. The patient was discharged after 10 days of recovery.

Treatment:

Following the diagnosis of stage III colorectal cancer, the patient was recommended to receive adjuvant chemotherapy with CAPOX starting 4 weeks after surgery. The selected regimen consisted of capecitabine and L-OHP. The anticancer drug dosage was reduced to 80% because of the patient's age. The patient also received 7.5 g of NYT daily throughout the course of adjuvant chemotherapy.

Outcome:

The patient did not report any significant adverse effects. Follow-up examination did not show any recurrence during a 1-year postoperative follow-up.

Discharge Condition:

The patient was discharged in stable condition with prescribed medications and follow-up appointment schedules.

Discharge Medications:

Detailed medication list not provided in the case report.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The principal diagnosis is malignant neoplasm of the sigmoid colon. In ICD-10-AM, C18 covers malignant neoplasm of the colon, and C18.7 is the sigmoid colon. The cancer was found through fecal occult blood, confirmed on colonoscopy and biopsy, and treated with laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy. The 23 cm distance from the anal verge fits the sigmoid colon, not the rectosigmoid junction (C19).

CODE: C18
